questions.prompt: When a modifying word ends in a vowel (e.g. 'maganda'), which linker form is attached directly to the end of the word?
questions.explanation: If the preceding word ends in a vowel, '-ng' is attached directly: maganda + -ng = magandang.

questions.prompt: When a modifying word ends in a consonant except 'n' (e.g. 'mabait'), which standalone linker is used?
questions.explanation: If the preceding word ends in a consonant (other than n), 'na' is placed as a separate word: mabait na bata.

questions.prompt: When a word ends in the letter 'n' (e.g. 'hangin'), how is the linker applied?
questions.explanation: If a word ends in 'n', the 'n' drops and is replaced by '-ng': hangin + -ng = hanging malamig.

questions.prompt: What is the Tagalog conjunction for 'and'? ______
What is the primary function of linkers (na/-ng) in Tagalog?
options: To connect modifiers (adjectives/nouns) to the words they modify
To mark the subject of a sentence
questions.correct_answer: To connect modifiers (adjectives/nouns) to the words they modify
questions.explanation: Linkers (na/-ng) join adjectives to nouns or adverbs to verbs to form coherent noun phrases or clauses.
